[[Carlos Alcaraz]] defeated [[Ben Shelton]] in the final, 7–6<sup>(7–5)</sup>, 7–5, to win the singles title at the [[2026 Rolex Paris Masters|2026 Paris Masters]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.rolexparismasters.com/en/news/article/final-carlos-alcaraz-victory-ben-shelton |title= Alcaraz, Paris’ young prince|publisher=rolexparismasters.com|accessdate=8 November 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://supersport.com/tennis/news/1c6f7709-9e88-43fc-84d5-c77a9c46a39c/alcaraz-wins-paris-masters-for-first-time|title=Alcaraz wins Paris Masters for first time|publisher=supersport.com|accessdate=8 November 2026}}</ref> It was his ninth [[ATP Masters 1000 tournaments|ATP Masters 1000]] title and 29th [[ATP Tour]] title overall. He saved two match points en route to the title, against [[Taylor Fritz]] in the quarterfinals. Alcaraz was the second Spaniard to win the title, following [[David Ferrer]] in [[2012 BNP Paribas Masters – Singles|2012]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/alcaraz-shelton-paris-2026-final-sunday|title=Alcaraz downs Shelton to win first Paris title|publisher=atptour.com|accessdate=8 November 2026}}</ref>

[[Jannik Sinner]] was the reigning champion,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/tennis/jannik-sinner-paris-masters-result-alcaraz-no-1-b2856978.html|title=Jannik Sinner reclaims World No 1 from Carlos Alcaraz with Paris Masters title|publisher=The Independent|accessdate=2 November 2025}}</ref> but withdrew before the tournament began due to a knee injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/sinner-2026-injury-announcement-october|title=Sinner to miss rest of 2026 due to injury|website=atptour.com|date=6 October 2026}}</ref>
 
This marked the first tournament played by [[Alexander Zverev]] as the incumbent [[List of ATP number 1 ranked singles tennis players|world No. 1]]. With his second-round defeat to [[Lorenzo Musetti]], Zverev became the fifth player (since the introduction of the [[ATP rankings]]) to lose their opening match played as world No. 1, and the first to lose their opening match as world No. 1 in straight sets.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://tennishead.net/the-four-other-men-who-lost-their-first-match-as-world-number-one-after-alexander-zverevs-paris-masters-loss/ |title= The four other men who lost their first match as world number one after Alexander Zverev’s Paris Masters loss |date=5 November 2026}}</ref>

[[Nuno Borges (tennis)|Nuno Borges]] became the first lucky loser to reach the [[Paris Masters]] quarterfinals.<ref> {{cite tweet|url=https://x.com/josemorgado/status/2118393677802528962|number= 2118393677802528962 |user=josemorgado|title= Nuno Borges easily beats Ignacio Buse 6-0, 6-2 to reach the BIGGEST QFs OF HIS CAREER in Paris. 1st EVER lucky loser to reach the Paris QFs, 3rd ever portuguese player to reach a singles QF at a Masters 1000…}} </ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://en.tennistemple.com/actu/rolex-paris-masters-nuno-borges-becomes-first/suLB|title= Rolex Paris Masters: Nuno Borges becomes first lucky loser to reach quarterfinals| date=5 November 2025}}</ref>
